bib.title: MEMAGENT: RESHAPING LONG-CONTEXT LLM WITH MULTI-CONV RL-BASED MEMORY AGENT

question: Can an LLM with a fixed small window process arbitrarily long documents at linear cost without losing accuracy, if it learns by RL what to keep in an overwritten memory?
hypothesis: End-to-end RL on the final-answer reward teaches the model to preserve and track critical information, avoiding information overwriting and lost-in-the-middle problems.
contributions: A novel approach that enables LLMs to process arbitrarily long inputs within a limited context window under linear time complexity during inference
An agent workflow implementing this mechanism with end-to-end training via multi-conversation DAPO
Empirical demonstration that the RL-trained method extrapolates to vastly long documents with minimal degradation

method.summary: The model reads a document chunk by chunk, each step seeing the question, the next chunk and a fixed-length memory, and overwrites the memory with newly generated tokens; a final step answers from the memory only. Memory updates are trained with Multi-Conv DAPO, which treats each independent-context conversation as a sample and applies the final-answer reward advantage to all of them.
method.task: long-context question answering and summarisation by memory-agent workflow with RL

datasets.name: Synthetic HotpotQA long-context QA (stage I)
datasets.size: 32,768 instances, each approximately 32K tokens (appendix also says about 28K, 200 articles each)
datasets.source: HotpotQA train split with RULER method: gold paragraphs among distractors from the same dataset
datasets.preprocessing: Questions dropped where Qwen2.5-7B-Base or -Instruct hits 100% Best-Of-2 with no context; 80,000 samples processed, about 50% filtered

datasets.name: Stage II mix: DocQA-RL-1.6K plus stage I data
datasets.source: DocQA-RL-1.6K from Wan et al. 2025 mixed with stage I data

datasets.name: RULER-HQA synthetic test sets
datasets.size: 128 samples per length (inferred: validation set synthesized with 128 samples and Table 1 values are multiples of 1/128); lengths 7K to 3.5M, 50 to 6400 wiki items
datasets.preprocessing: Number of wiki items 50 to 6400 gives about 7K to 3.5M tokens

datasets.name: LongBench-QA
datasets.size: five subsets (2Wiki, HQA, MuSiQue, NQA, Qasper); items per subset not stated
datasets.source: NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue from LongBench

datasets.name: NIAH (RULER niah_single_1, _2, _3)
datasets.size: 8K to 512K; items per level not stated (Fig 5 values are multiples of 1/128 per level, inferred)
datasets.source: RULER; level 1 repeated sentences with 7-digit needle, level 2 essays, level 3 essays with 36-char UUID needle

models.name: RL-MemAgent-14B
models.architecture: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, unchanged architecture and positional embeddings
models.context: 8K window: 1024 query, 5000 chunk, 1024 memory, 1024 output, rest for chat template

other.setup: 5,000-token chunks for memory creation, top 30 memories at retrieval; results for Mem0 are named in D.2 but no Mem0 table appears in the text
K=2,4,6,8 on RULER-HQA (wiki item chunks); chunk C=1024 or 2048 and K=2..8 on LongBench-QA

training.objective: Multi-Conv DAPO: token-level clipped policy loss over (group, conversation, token), outcome reward R=1[is_equiv(y,y_hat)] from a rule-based verifier; advantage A=R_i-mean(R) without std division (Dr. GRPO), from the final conversation, applied to all conversations of that sample
training.batch_size: rollout batch size 256, group size 16; actual mini-batch size differs because of multiple conversations; ratio of sample batch to backprop batch 16 (off-policy)
training.steps: stage I about 400 steps until converged; stage II steps not stated
training.seq_len: 8K window per conversation; documents up to 60K tokens in training

other.curriculum: two stages: stage I basic memory capability, stage II transfer to more diverse contexts and harder tasks
other.clip: epsilon_low and epsilon_high used but values not given

inference.max_tokens: 1024 output per turn in MemAgent; baselines 10,000 output
inference.samples: not stated; single run per cell inferred
inference.prompting: Two templates: context-processing (problem, memory, section -> Updated memory) and answer generation (problem, memory -> \boxed{}); evaluation asks for 'the answer is ANSWER.'
inference.retrieval: none for MemAgent; RAG baselines use text-embedding-3-large with cosine similarity top-K

parameters.memory_ablation: 256 to 4096; context chunks adjusted so memory+chunk is constant (m4096-c1928, m3072-c2952, m2048-c3976, m1024-c5000)

metrics.name: sub_em accuracy
metrics.definition: answer correct if it contains all elements of the ground truth; multi-part answers score proportion correct; answers normalised (articles removed, case ignored); extracted by regex

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L recall
metrics.definition: recall scores on GovReport and QMSum

eval.protocol: Accuracy at lengths 7K to 896K for all models; 1.75M and 3.5M only for MemAgent. No seeds, intervals or significance tests reported.

availability.code: promised: 'will be available in open-source platforms'

prompts.text:
You are presented with a problem, a section of an article that may contain the answer, and a previous memory. Please read the section carefully and update the memory with new information that helps to answer the problem, while retaining all relevant details from the previous memory.
<problem> {prompt} </problem>
<memory> {memory} </memory>
<section> {chunk} </section>
Updated memory:

You are presented with a problem and a previous memory. Please answer the problem based on the previous memory and put the answer in \boxed {}.
<problem> {prompt} </problem>
<memory> {memory} </memory>
Your answer:

limits: No hardware, GPU hours, seeds, decoding temperature or run count reported; no confidence intervals.
Stage I data size described as about 32K tokens and about 28K tokens in two places.
The authors show failure patterns: information overwritten when memory fills, missing critical information in multi-hop questions, primacy bias (App F).
Evaluation is mostly synthetic (RULER-HQA built like stage I training data, NIAH); natural-text tests (LongBench) are short.
Compared on RULER-HQA only against RAG at K<=8; Mem0 baseline named but no Mem0 results table in the text.
Code, data and weights promised, not linked in the text.

terms.definition: After reading a new chunk, the model overwrites the previous memory with an updated one of fixed length
DAPO extended to a (group, conversation, token) structure so each context-independent conversation of a rollout is optimised, with the reward from the final answer
